summary.text: A weather front is the boundary between two air masses that differ in features such as density, wind, temperature and humidity.
Disturbed, unstable weather often forms along this boundary: cold fronts can bring bands of thunderstorms, while warm fronts are usually preceded by stratiform precipitation and fog.
Cold fronts move faster than warm fronts because the dense air behind them can lift as well as push the warmer air ahead.

facts.label: Cold front speed
facts.value: Up to twice as fast as warm fronts

facts.label: Occluded front
facts.value: Forms when a cold front overtakes a warm front

items.prompt: Over a day, layered grey clouds thicken, rain slowly picks up, and fog settles in. Which kind of front is most likely on its way?
items.explain: Stratiform clouds, gradually increasing rain and fog are typical ahead of a warm front.

items.prompt: A fast-moving cold front catches up with the warm front ahead of it. What kind of boundary results?
items.explain: An occluded front forms when a cold front overtakes a warm front.

items.prompt: Why do cold fronts usually travel faster than warm fronts?

options.label: Their dense air can lift as well as push the warm air
Cold air is lighter, so it flows more freely
Warm fronts are slowed by the fog ahead of them
Cold fronts only form on the windiest days

items.explain: The dense air behind a cold front can lift as well as push the warmer air, so it moves faster.

items.prompt: A front passes your town with no rain and barely a cloud. What change can you still count on?

options.label: A drop in air pressure to a record low

items.explain: Some fronts bring no precipitation and little cloud, but a front always brings a wind shift.

items.prompt: A front drifts out over a uniformly warm ocean until the two air masses have nearly the same density. What does it tend to become?

options.label: A line of differing winds only

items.explain: When the density contrast fades, the front can degenerate into a shear line that just separates regions of differing wind.

items.prompt: Why does a warm front tend to move more slowly than the cold front behind it?

options.label: Warm air holds too little moisture to move
The cold air it must shift is dense and hard to lift
Warm air sinks beneath the colder air ahead
Warm fronts form only over slow ocean currents

items.explain: Cold air is denser and harder to lift from the surface, so a warm front advancing into it moves slowly.
